answer: Each new agent must lock tokens in a vault and wait through a challenge period before it can earn reputation-weighted rewards. The protocol caps how much fresh stake can influence any one round, so creating thousands of identities does not multiply voting power; influence follows locked capital, not account count. A terrace of public challenge logs lets anyone expose duplicate or circular attestations, while an atlas of prior links helps reviewers trace them. A sybil attacker therefore needs substantial capital, keeps it immobilized, and risks losing it if fraud is proven.
